exposure: birth during the first peak of the coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19) pandemic
cohort: 588 infants born between February and March of 2019 (pre-COVID-19 group) and 2020 (COVID-19 group)
finding: Infants born during the first peak of the COVID-19 pandemic (February-March 2020) had a significantly lower incidence of wheezing, bronchodilator use, systemic steroid use, emergency room visits, LRTI admissions, and pneumonia diagnoses compared to infants born during the same period in the previous year.
mod_finding: The study does not mention any findings related to mode of delivery.
